patterns: 21st Sectors Donut (catalog component 20086) adapted as a dependency-free interactive B20-universe count, with linked SVG arcs and legend rows.
21st Currency Exchange Card (catalog component 8204) adapted as a native Base v4 buy panel backed by server-side Uniswap quote and swap routes.

21st Data Table (catalog component 27049) interaction pattern, search plus quick-filter pills with counts plus sortable headers, adapted as a dependency-free toolbar over the /stocks hub's server-rendered rows.

must: Keep pre-launch states explicit; never present placeholder figures as live protocol data.
Use Base blue as the primary brand signal with accessible high-contrast type.
avoid: Generic crypto-dashboard visual language, gradients, and simulated live metrics.
Claims of trustlessness where keeper or owner operation remains involved.

decisions.reason: Keep the compact utility navigation and footer, while moving the content to a Space Grotesk-only, Base-blue market system with square-edged data surfaces and no display-serif editorial treatment.
The selected 21st Sectors Donut interaction is adapted for the 13-title B20 universe; it reports title counts rather than suggesting an unapproved allocation or live market data.

The home now prioritizes the buy module and the active B20 universe, removing the editorial ownership panel. The swap component only exposes executable API states and clearly shows when the BASKET custom-hook pool has not been configured or routed.

Documentation is a compact public protocol reference built from the actual Solidity and keeper implementation, with a static contents rail informed by the 21st Table of Content exploration (catalog component 22596). It favors contract functions, state transitions, market mechanics, controls and limitations over marketing copy or frontend configuration.

decisions.choice: Hub table as a lookup tool
decisions.reason: At 43 listings the /stocks table gains search (ticker, name or contract address), All / Minted / Trading views that open on Minted, and sortable header cells with a native sort select below 860px. The resting order stays the server's (deepest market first); the premium sorts discount-first; nulls never win a sort.
